content_summary.bill: Assembly No. 5386, 222nd Legislature (2026-2027 session), INTRODUCED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 (per bill header). Synopsis: 'Requires EDA to coordinate study of financing mechanisms and recommendations for supplemental funding of certain public transit projects.' Long title: 'An Act requiring the study of financing mechanisms and recommendations for supplemental funding of certain public transit projects.'
content_summary.sponsors: Assemblywoman Katie Brennan, District 32 (Hudson); Assemblyman Clinton Calabrese, District 36 (Bergen and Passaic) (bill cover page). Calabrese is District 36, NOT District 32 as the scanner/article state (the article itself says D-32 for Calabrese; the bill says 36). Brennan is Assemblywoman, not 'Assemblyman'.
content_summary.what_it_directs: s.2a: NJEDA 'shall, in consultation with the Division of Taxation in the Department of the Treasury and public transit operators, develop a report to study and make recommendations concerning the various financing mechanisms that could be implemented by the State to generate supplemental public transit funding'; at least one public hearing before publication. s.2b lists ten items to cover per mechanism (revenue estimates and sustainability; economic effects on State/local finances; mandatory vs optional; conditions such as 'areas in need of redevelopment, low-density zoning, or a major capital investment'; restricted/dedicated revenue; who implements; beneficiaries; 'logistical or legal challenges ... including ... constitutional limitations'; overlap with other incentives). s.2c: written report to Governor and Legislature, published on the Authority's website. s.2d: 'The Commissioner of Community Affairs shall publish guidance or model ordinances to assist municipalities in implementing any of the recommendations contained in the report' (so DCA guidance is in the bill, but conditional on report recommendations and after publication). s.3: takes effect immediately.
content_summary.instruments_and_definitions: s.1 'Value capture' means 'strategies implemented by the State or a local government to recover a portion of the value created by public transit community development' and 'may include, but shall not be limited to, tax increment financing, special assessments, joint development by public and private entities, and development impact fees.' 'Financing mechanism' is broader than value capture: also bond financing/securitization, payments in lieu of property taxes, ground-lease revenues, zoning/permitting revenues incl. air rights, and economic development incentives. No tax on land value, land value tax, or split-rate is named anywhere in the text. 'Public transit operator' = NJ Transit Corporation and the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation (PATH), and may include other operators incl. a bi-state entity.
content_summary.deadlines_appropriation: No deadline for the report, hearing or DCA guidance. No appropriation. No mandate to adopt any mechanism; study and recommendations only.
content_summary.committee_referral: Not obtained (not in the introduced text; status page unreadable without JavaScript). Do not state a referral.
content_summary.sponsor_rationale: The bill's own Statement is descriptive (restates the study duty and definitions) and gives no rationale or station examples. The rationale (land near new stations gains value created by transit; 'This could unlock billions of dollars'; Hudson-Bergen Light Rail extension to Bergen County, Newark and Paterson; Glassboro-Camden line; proposed infill stations at 18th Street Jersey City and 15th Street Hoboken; TIF and special-assessment explainer; Chicago Red Line TIF; Fairfax County special assessment for Silver Line) appears only in the Hudson County View article quoting Brennan and an explainer video (not fetched) -- B/C, origin only.
content_summary.timing: Bill introduced 10 Sept 2026; the article (16 Nov 2026) reports the sponsor's explainer-video launch two months later and describes the bill as newly introduced. Date wording on the wiki should be 'introduced in September 2026'.
